nodes.label: Viewsical 0.1.7 release changes
nodes.description: 18 November 2026 Windows x64 release documents shared controls, scroll behavior, five-point volume, final-queue seeking, normalization, hidden outer scrollbar, retired Lua cleanup, adapter modules and refreshed Graphify.

nodes.label: Persistent audio-only default
nodes.description: Always start with audio only persists across restarts; changing the current item to video leaves that default intact. Mode changes preserve position and pause intent.

nodes.label: Dedicated remembered Google sign-in
nodes.description: Dedicated WebView2 profile stores persistent cookies; session cookies have a current-user DPAPI fallback. Startup validates saved sessions, transient failures retain them, and sign-out removes them.

nodes.label: Installer and portable delivery
nodes.description: GitHub releases offer a Windows x64 per-user NSIS installer and portable ZIP with SHA256SUMS.txt. Extract the entire portable archive and retain tools and ytdlp-plugins beside Viewsical.exe. WebView2 Runtime is required and can be obtained by the installer; bundled media helpers avoid dependence on system Python, FFmpeg or mpv.

nodes.label: Watch scrolling and Back to top
nodes.description: Scrolling keeps visible native video clipped below the fixed header without changing source or position. Search uses a circular submit button; Home and playlist pages offer Back to top with reduced-motion and player spacing support.
nodes.norm_label: watch scrolling and back to top

nodes.label: Retired Lua renderer upgrade cleanup
nodes.description: The retired Lua controls renderer is removed and its installed resource is cleaned up during upgrades.

nodes.label: TubeDesk former product name
nodes.description: TubeDesk is the former name of Viewsical. The original app.tubedesk.desktop identifier remains so existing user data continues through the rename.

nodes.label: Viewsical 0.1.7
nodes.description: Windows desktop video player built with Tauri 2, Rust, React and TypeScript; formerly TubeDesk.

nodes.label: Latest GitHub release downloads
nodes.description: Windows x64 installer, portable ZIP and SHA256SUMS.txt are available from the latest release.

nodes.label: Queryable codebase map
nodes.description: graphify-out/graph.html is the interactive map, graph.json is the queryable graph, and GRAPH_REPORT.md records communities and relationship evidence. Coverage includes app source, tests, scripts, design/runtime docs and artwork; generated builds, tool binaries, dependency caches and duplicate Windows icon exports are excluded.

nodes.label: Focused YouTube adapter modules
nodes.description: youtube.rs and youtube/ form the replaceable yt-dlp boundary, split by request lifecycle, helper execution, browsing, playback sources, identity, metadata and errors.

nodes.label: Behavior-preserving YouTube adapter refactor
nodes.rationale: Split the adapter into focused Rust modules while preserving its public interface and function behavior.

nodes.label: Bounded main-window shutdown
nodes.rationale: Closing the main window initiates bounded extraction, download, mpv and WebView shutdown while preserving the sign-in profile.

nodes.label: Embedded Google sign-in limitation
nodes.rationale: Google can reject embedded sign-in. The app reports the limitation, retains anonymous features and does not represent blocked login as connected.

nodes.label: Scroll-triggered pagination
nodes.rationale: Home, Search, library lists and playlists fetch another page near the list end. Playlist queues retain their loaded portion and fetch near the queue bottom or when playback approaches its last loaded item; starting a playlist does not load all contents. Load more / Retry remains available.

nodes.label: Local playback history
nodes.rationale: SQLite keeps guest/account local history separate. Local playback history is distinct from YouTube watch history and the app does not intentionally report remote progress. Signing out removes private local history; clearing media cache preserves it.

nodes.label: Pinned bundled media helpers
nodes.rationale: Setup downloads pinned yt-dlp, Deno, mpv, FFmpeg and FFprobe, verifies available archive checksums and records binary SHA-256 values. Releases bundle the helpers; adapter updates require explicit source/build changes.

nodes.label: Incremental playlist queues
nodes.rationale: Keep loaded playlist occurrences, including repeated videos, and fetch near the queue end instead of loading the entire playlist at startup. Docking preserves source and position.

nodes.label: Isolated account WebView
nodes.rationale: Google sign-in uses a dedicated app WebView/profile without external-browser cookie import or an app-owned password form. Remote sign-in pages have no privileged Tauri capabilities. Temporary cookie files are current-user restricted and removed after helper operations or swept after a crash; logs omit cookies and resolved stream URLs.

nodes.label: Stable app.tubedesk.desktop identity
nodes.rationale: Retain the original internal identifier through the Viewsical rename so existing sign-in, settings, cache and history continue to work. Persistent records use stable video IDs instead of expiring stream URLs.

nodes.label: Validated persistent media cache
nodes.description: Cache complete components only after track/duration validation, reuse them across restarts, and evict older unused media under a default 2 GB limit. Active-file deletion waits for player release; explicit downloads remain permanent.

nodes.label: Embedded native playback
nodes.description: Native child-window playback uses mpv IPC with selection, position restoration and bounded recovery. Floating and bottom-docked playback preserve source and position. The current shared React controls appear in one reusable transparent WebView above mpv; scrolling clips visible video beneath the fixed header without changing its size or position.

nodes.label: Persistent resumable downloads
nodes.description: Video/audio downloads can pause, resume, play or reveal completed files, which remain available offline. Persistent jobs refresh sources on resume, retain partial files, merge and validate with FFprobe. MP4 requires H.264/AAC availability; MKV accepts other source codecs, while audio downloads preserve the selected source format.

nodes.label: Namida public orchestration reference
nodes.rationale: Use public app responsibilities as reference without copying unavailable private youtipie implementation or treating inferred protocol details as requirements.

nodes.label: Native decoder and output evidence
nodes.rationale: Decoded/output operation and non-silent cached signals are demonstrated, while physical speaker recording is not claimed.

nodes.label: TubeDesk versioned verification evidence
nodes.rationale: The document records earlier-release checks separately from the current renamed source and states what each check establishes.

nodes.label: Verified native audio readiness
nodes.rationale: Video restart alone does not establish sound. Readiness also requires selected expected audio, decoder parameters and active output while preserving intentional mute/volume.

nodes.label: Disposable cache boundary
nodes.rationale: Internal cache can be evicted and full-source caching consumes additional bandwidth; explicit Downloads provide intentional permanent storage.

nodes.label: Pinned cache file leases
nodes.rationale: Clearing retires entries immediately but delays byte deletion until the native player closes pinned files; eviction targets older unpinned entries.

nodes.label: Current-load stale-work guard
nodes.rationale: New load identities prevent old extraction, native entry events and recovery attempts from committing to a newer selection.

nodes.label: Local-first source selection
nodes.rationale: Try completed downloads, then validated internal components, then online extraction; explicit quality changes may bypass a lower-quality local source.

nodes.label: FFprobe publication gate
nodes.rationale: Partial files cannot become reusable offline entries until expected tracks and complete duration are validated.

nodes.label: Stable media identity
nodes.rationale: Reusable local media must survive expiring extraction URLs; persisted indexes omit signed URLs, headers and cookies.

nodes.label: Explicit verification limits
nodes.rationale: Historical tests do not certify every DPI, disk-full, expiry, codec or provider-policy case; installer compilation is distinguished from installation.

nodes.label: Audio normalization policy and historical 0.1.5 player changes
nodes.description: Gain policy remains current; ASS/Lua controls and associated 0.1.5 native-control verification are historical and superseded by shared React controls in 0.1.6.
nodes.norm_label: audio normalization policy and historical 0.1.5 player changes

nodes.label: Historical 0.1.5 ASS/Lua controls
nodes.description: Historical physical-pixel ASS fades and native translucent settings menus. Viewsical 0.1.6 replaced these controls with shared React controls; this section does not describe the current renderer.

nodes.label: mpv volume-gain
nodes.description: Per-file dB gain remains separate from user volume, mute, speed, position and pause intent; no re-encoding or filter-chain rebuild.

nodes.label: Viewsical yt-dlp loudness plugin
nodes.description: Pinned yt-dlp 2026.10.26 extractor hook reads playerConfig.audioConfig.loudnessDb only when the response video ID matches the requested item. Context-local scope handles reuse, nesting, concurrency and exceptions. Only the application-owned plugin directory is enabled.

nodes.label: MediaItem.youtubeLoudnessDb metadata
nodes.description: Rust revalidates optional loudness metadata and preserves only the stable numeric value in cache/download records for offline gain; legacy records use neutral gain and downloaded bytes remain unchanged.

nodes.label: Five-point volume keyboard shortcuts
nodes.description: Up/Down changes app volume by five percentage points, including paused and bottom-docked playback. Text fields, menus and dialogs keep normal arrows; volume remains separate from mute and normalization.

nodes.label: Attenuation-only loudness normalization
nodes.rationale: For finite loudness metadata in [-100,100] dB, enabled playback applies clamp(-loudness_db,-20,0) dB. No boost avoids adding clipping without a measured peak or limiter; missing/invalid metadata and disabled normalization use 0 dB. This is not waveform analysis or a guaranteed LUFS target.

nodes.label: Guarded normalization source commits
nodes.rationale: Explicit volume-gain file options reset missing metadata to zero. Selection/load/session guards reject stale results; settings changes serialize with source commits, and file-loaded rechecks settings to cover changes during opening.

nodes.label: Independent main-window maximization state
nodes.rationale: SQLite ui_state restores maximized/restored state before showing the window. Fullscreen, minimized and hidden states, frontend settings and account changes cannot replace that normal-window choice.

nodes.label: Final queue item EOF recovery
nodes.rationale: Natural EOF unloads mpv. Seeking or toggling the final item reopens the same queue occurrence at the requested position or zero while retaining mode, quality and queue identity; local cache/download sources and regular normalization commits remain eligible.

nodes.label: Serialized five-point volume actions
nodes.rationale: Rust serializes exactly ±5-point changes against current state and persists the clamped result independently of normalization/mute. Shortcut classification preserves editable/menu/dialog arrows and horizontal range controls; no second mpv native key handler runs.

nodes.label: Independent playback loudness normalization
nodes.rationale: Default-on playback gain uses YouTube loudness metadata, attenuating at most 20 dB without boosting quiet tracks. Missing metadata applies neutral gain; user volume and original media files remain unchanged, while cache/download metadata can retain correction.

nodes.label: Remembered main-window maximization
nodes.rationale: Restore the last normal maximized choice at startup; fullscreen and minimization must not overwrite it.

nodes.label: Shared React playback controls in Viewsical 0.1.6
nodes.description: Current control architecture, replacing the historical native ASS/Lua renderer.
nodes.norm_label: shared react playback controls in viewsical 0.1.6

nodes.label: PlayerOverlay.tsx controls-only presentation
nodes.description: Mounts only PlayerControls, without a second application shell.

nodes.label: PlayerControls.tsx shared playback controls
nodes.description: One React control set supplies transport, seeking, volume and settings for audio, video and docking, with Roboto, Lucide SVG icons and translucent rounded menus. CSS gradients replace ASS strips; Lua renderer is removed from source and packaging.

nodes.label: Reusable transparent controls WebView host
nodes.description: Rust lazily creates one transparent, frameless, shadowless WebView owned by the main window. Deduplicated physical bounds track move/resize/DPI/focus/scroll/fullscreen. Hiding follows mode, docking, dialogs and lifecycle; successful local presentation handshake reveals it.

nodes.label: Restricted overlay capability boundary
nodes.rationale: Only the bundled origin/path may navigate. Capabilities permit event listening, presentation snapshots and typed playback actions; account, browsing, download, storage and window commands remain inaccessible. Stable metadata/state/revision/loadId cross the boundary, cookies and temporary URLs stay in Rust, and stale-load actions fail. Main coordinator owns queue navigation, fullscreen, theater and scrolling.

nodes.label: Playback progress and control gesture lifecycle
nodes.norm_label: playback progress and control gesture lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Approximately 5 Hz broadcasts feed local requestAnimationFrame interpolation only for visible playing controls. Pointer leave dismisses menus; menus/gestures prevent inactivity hiding, and cancelled or cross-load gestures cannot seek.

nodes.label: Release QA identity and verification limits
nodes.norm_label: release qa identity and verification limits
nodes.rationale: Optimized native testing uses a compiled app.viewsical.v016qa identity, explicit QA data directory and verified executable ID, rather than the debug-only data override. Actual portable resources/single-instance/closure are checked separately. Native composition was verified at actual 125% Windows scale; browser density emulation is not native DPI certification.

nodes.label: Retry controls overlay recovery
nodes.rationale: Renderer failure leaves main-window keyboard controls available. Retry waits for Tauri to remove the destroyed window before reusing its label, preventing skipped recreation; verification confirms one replacement overlay with unchanged playback load/gain.

nodes.label: Historical Viewsical 0.1.5 Electron assessment
nodes.description: Architecture and test observations are from 0.1.5, including obsolete ASS/Lua controls and 17 frontend tests; no comparative runtime benchmark was performed.

nodes.label: Historical PlayerManager coordination reference
nodes.description: Memory cites src-tauri/src/player.rs L164 from an old graph; location is not current-source evidence.

nodes.label: Historical PlaybackPlan reference
nodes.description: Memory cites src-tauri/src/youtube.rs L28 from an old graph; location requires verification.

nodes.label: Historical 0.1.5 playback coordination query
nodes.description: Old graph locations predate edits and require current-source verification; records the former Rust source-commit and separate native-control boundaries.

nodes.label: Historical tubedesk_osc.lua renderer reference
nodes.description: Old memory cites resources/player/tubedesk_osc.lua L1 for the former separate native control boundary; this is a historical graph reference, not current-source evidence.

nodes.label: Historical recommendation to retain Tauri
nodes.rationale: Retain Tauri for the existing Windows app unless a measured prototype shows a specific advantage or TypeScript backend maintenance is a priority. Electron may simplify JavaScript/session integration and provide controlled Chromium, while native playback composition, extraction failures and embedded Google sign-in remain separate problems.

nodes.label: Historical shell migration proposal
nodes.rationale: A shell migration could retain Rust media logic as a service after decoupling AppHandle, events, paths and native window ownership. Preserve SQLite/cache data and plan authentication migration; yt-dlp, Deno, FFmpeg, FFprobe and mpv remain dependencies when only the shell changes.

nodes.label: Native clipping and navigation verification
nodes.description: Four frontend geometry tests, two Rust clipping tests, regressions, native region diagnostics and screenshot inspection verify identical regions, unchanged video dimensions/load ID and restoration without reload. Native inspection used 125% Windows scale; browser layouts cover 100%,125%,150%,200% density.

nodes.label: Search submit and Back to top controls
nodes.description: Separate accessible 46px circular search submit; Home remains in sidebar and logo. Home and individual playlists show Back to top after 320px, respect reduced motion, focus the heading, retain loaded pages and avoid floating/bottom players.
nodes.norm_label: search submit and back to top controls

nodes.label: 0.1.7 verification record
nodes.description: The changelog records 61 Rust tests, 26 frontend unit tests and 10 isolated live app checks, including actual video/audio playback, normalization, cache replay, completed audio download and restart behavior. Further native/browser layout coverage is recorded in shared-player and scrolling docs.

nodes.label: Shared native visible clipping
nodes.rationale: playerViewport.ts sends the original physical rectangle and actual header bottom; player_geometry::visible_clip intersects it with the available client viewport. Both mpv and controls receive the same rounded clipped region, preserving video size, playback position and load while scrolling. Fully offscreen, audio-only, docked and blocked surfaces hide; fullscreen uses the entire client viewport.

nodes.label: Bounded read-only YouTube comments
nodes.description: Top/Newest pages contain 20 comments, bounded to 300 per order and cached until closure; no posting, liking or replying.

nodes.label: Stable comment-anchor pagination
nodes.rationale: The CLI exposes no reusable provider continuation, so bounded prefix re-extraction locates a stable final-comment ID; missing anchors request refresh and UI deduplicates shifting results.

nodes.label: Session-generation invalidation
nodes.rationale: Account changes invalidate account media and private metadata; comment cursors bind to session generation as well as video and sort.

nodes.label: In-memory browsing pages
nodes.rationale: Retain visited pages, loaded items and scroll position until app closure; failed reload preserves the previous page, while account changes clear incompatible views.

nodes.label: Tauri Rust React stack
nodes.description: Viewsical is a Windows desktop app built with Tauri 2, Rust, React and TypeScript. src contains the local UI, typed IPC bridge, queue, presentation and accessibility; the Rust backend coordinates native playback, sessions, downloads, cache, comments and SQLite storage.
